title: Rome condemned the view that freedom is opposed to compulsion only: Pius V and Gregory XIII
source_text: XXXVII. Verum ista sententia quae libertatem arbitrii statuit oppositam esse, non necessitati, sed coactioni tantum; a Pontificibus Romanis damnata est. Nam Bellarminus meminit decreti cujusdam Pii V. quod postea a Gregorio XIII. renovatum fuit, in quo inter alias multas propositiones, hae quoque censura notantur. Quod voluntarie fit, etiamsi necessitate fiat, libere tamen fit. Item, sola violentia repugnat libertati hominis naturali.
pass_a_gloss: But that opinion which states liberty of choice to be opposed, not to necessity, but to compulsion only, has been condemned by the Roman Pontiffs. For Bellarmine mentions a certain decree of Pius V. which was afterwards renewed by Gregory XIII. in which among many other propositions, these also are marked with censure. What is done voluntarily, even if it be done by necessity, is yet done freely. Likewise, violence alone is repugnant to the natural liberty of man.
pass_b_english: The view that freedom of choice is opposed only to compulsion and not to necessity has, however, been condemned by the popes of Rome.

Bellarmine mentions a decree of Pius V, later renewed by Gregory XIII, which censures these two propositions among many others: 'What is done voluntarily is done freely, even if it is done of necessity', and 'Only violence is incompatible with man's natural freedom.'

choices.why: Kept as in the preceding locus on free choice in general, so the Roman and Reformed accounts are compared in one vocabulary.
